### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — WO2 defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | No Inquiry-specific AI policy page found; journal follows the general Taylor & Francis group policy. Generative AI may not be listed as author; authors are accountable for content originality/integrity. Disclosure required: any use of Generative AI must be acknowledged in the article text with tool name, version, and reason for use. AI tools must not be used to generate/manipulate research data, images or figures. T&F's public guidance explicitly notes some journals restrict AI use beyond language polishing and tells authors to check the journal's own 'Instructions for Authors' — no Inquiry-specific restriction beyond the group policy was found in this search, so leniency is rated as the group default (3/5: allowed for idea generation/language/literature search with mandatory disclosure, banned for data/image generation and for authorship credit), not confirmed as journal-specific. |
| **Source URL** | https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/editorial-policies/using-ai-in-your-research-and-manuscript-preparations/ |

**Current positioning (WO2, what the journal accepts now):** General philosophy journal (metaphysics, epistemology, ethics, logic, aesthetics, philosophy of mind/language) publishing research articles, symposia, special issues, target articles, review essays, and critical discussions. Actively running a guest-edited special section 'Mind, Language, and AI: Philosophical Investigations into Large Language Models' (eds. Alex Grzankowski and Anandi Hattiangadi), plus a special section 'Linguistic Understanding: Perception and Inference' (eds. Anna Drożdżowicz and Kim Pedersen Phillips) — indicating current strong appetite for philosophy-of-AI/LLM and philosophy-of-language submissions. A 2025 article 'Publishing robots' (DOI 10.1080/0020174X.2025.2460764) also touches on AI/authorship themes, reinforcing this as a live topical area.

**Methods noted as welcome (WO2, qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** conceptual/argumentative philosophy papers, philosophy of mind and language, epistemology (including AI/LLM epistemology), metaphysics, ethics, aesthetics, philosophy of AI / large language models (currently topical via special section), critical discussion / review essay responding to existing literature
